THE THIRD DATUM COMPARISON, and the per-row dispositions of T17's 11 CANDIDATE rows. Two screens already exist and neither can decide an ORDER question: fndiff's datum MULTISET is blind to a transposition BY CONSTRUCTION (its own docstring says so), and es_named_reloc_census's row-set LABEL PERMUTATION test is all-or-nothing over its own differing rows, so ONE unrelated row destroys the permutation verdict for a pair that IS transposed. The third comparison is the whole ORDERED sequence of datum keys in relocation order -- but ONLY with the rule below attached, because the bare ordered compare is worse than useless on unmatched functions.

THE RULE. For an ordered mismatch at index i whose two datum keys also appear MIRRORED at some index j, read the REGISTER FIELD (the instruction's first register operand: the destination of a load or an lis/addi, the value written by a store) at the SAME POSITION on both sides.
  * CROSSED -- the target's register at i reappears in ours at j and vice versa. Each datum still reaches the SAME register; only the emission order moved. A SCHEDULE fact. Measured: game/game/gamemain::fn_80057024, target `lfs f1,255.0f` then `lfs f4,0.0f` against ours `lfs f4,0.0f` then `lfs f1,255.0f` -- f1 holds 255.0 and f4 holds 0.0 in BOTH streams.
  * SAME-SLOT -- the SAME register, at the SAME position, under the SAME mnemonic, receives a DIFFERENT datum. THE transposition. Measured: game/enemy/enemy::move_logic00, both streams `lfd f30`, target 400921fb54524550 (pi) and ours 401921fb54524550 (2pi) -- the exact bug fndiff names as its multiset's blind spot.
Three further exclusions, each with the count it removed: CONVERSION-MAGIC (a mirror involving 0x4330000000000000 / 0x4330000080000000, MWCC's own int<->float constants, whose position is a codegen fact) 8 rows; SHIFT (our key at i is the target's at i-d for one small d, i.e. a displaced relocation earlier in the stream) 130 rows; SPLIT-FORM (mirrored under two DIFFERENT mnemonics -- an @ha/@lo materialisation interleave) 54 rows. And a hard guard: when the datum MULTISETS differ the screen returns UNDECIDABLE and never BENIGN, because a value delta exists that an ordering screen does not adjudicate.

TWO-SIDED CALIBRATION at 5f9ef72ba. POSITIVE control, es_named_reloc_census's own 8 TRANSPOSED: 6 DEFECT, 2 UNDECIDABLE, 0 BENIGN. NEGATIVE control, its 7 WRONG-DATUM: 0 DEFECT, 7 UNDECIDABLE, 0 BENIGN -- it never contradicts the multiset screen and never issues a clean bill over a value delta. Its 2 TRANSPOSED?: both UNDECIDABLE. BASE RATE over every paired function in the image (3032): 12 DEFECT (0.40%), 2845 BENIGN, 175 UNDECIDABLE, 84 seconds. The 12 are generate_enemy(4), pbDiagDrawInfo(4), do_player_select(4), write_shop_menu(3), ReadControls(2), pbDiagDrawAudio(2), fn_800C7558(2), InitNameAudio(2), move_logic00(1), loadGauntletSave(1), draw_inventory_panel(1), do_sel_menu(1) -- FIVE of which (pbDiagDrawInfo, pbDiagDrawAudio, move_logic00, draw_inventory_panel, do_sel_menu) es_named_reloc_census never nominated at all, because it pairs only lbl_*-against-lbl_* rows at the same index while this screen resolves every relocation symbol including named globals and @N pool entries.

THE 11 CANDIDATE DISPOSITIONS (T17's question, answered): 1 DEFECT, 3 BENIGN, 7 UNDECIDABLE.
  DEFECT      game/sys/memcard::loadGauntletSave -- reloc [162], target `stw r0,lbl_80344A14` against ours `stw r0,lbl_80344A18`, mirrored at [161] where the target stores r3 to A18 and we store r29 to A14. The same value register writes the OTHER .sbss word: two adjacent uninitialised globals swapped, invisible to real, --clean, the set delta, fuzzy and the multiset. A SOURCE item for whoever owns game/sys/memcard.
  BENIGN      game/pb/pb_frame::pbFrameMode -- the ordered datum sequences are IDENTICAL end to end, so no transposition exists anywhere in the function and CANDIDATE was the whole story.
  BENIGN      game/game/gamemain::do_stats_display -- both mirrored rows are the int<->float conversion magic against 42700000 (60.0f).
  BENIGN      game/shop/shop::show_gold -- likewise, the magic against 3f70000000000000 (1/256).
  UNDECIDABLE game/boss/bosscam::BossCamPlayerCalc, game/game/gamemain::fn_80057024, game/ui/select::setup_vmu_entries (2 split-form rows each: an @ha/@lo interleave); game/pb/pb_objregs::sDrawGeom, game/ui/select::serve_blits (unpaired rows behind a 2- or 3-place shift run); game/world/camera::camera_collide_step (1 unpaired + 2 split-form); game/world/gauntworld::fn_800606FC (3 unpaired + 2 split-form + 2 address-only).
Note what this does to T17's own framing: its cheapest_refuting_observation ('if the ordered datum sequences are identical then no transposition exists and CANDIDATE is the whole story; run it over all 11 in one pass with fndiff.datum_relocs') is only executable on ONE of the 11 -- the other 10 have differing instruction streams, where a bare index compare both misses real swaps and manufactures fake ones. Run bare, it returns 1 BENIGN and 10 UNDECIDABLE; run with a naive mirror search and no register rule, it returns 8 DEFECT, five of which are pure reorders.
